findings: BTZ_1.tex:1593 ('(ii) => (i) is a consequence of Proposition prop:reg_complete'): a missing step, not an error. prop:reg_complete gives the conclusion for Reg of the extension N, not of M; carrying it back needs (a) that a BTZ-embedding maps Reg M onto Reg N (types of points are preserved, and the complement of the image is BTZ), (b) that this restriction is an isometry of flat spacetimes, and (c) that global hyperbolicity, Cauchy-maximality and Cauchy-completeness (the image surface is a Cauchy surface, spacelike Lipschitz in the target charts, with isometric induced length spaces) are invariant under flat isometries. Supplied and proved (GX.BTZCauchyEasy.regM_of_isBTZEmbedding and the transport lemmas).

BTZ_1.tex:1582-1593: the standing hypothesis 'M globally hyperbolic' is used by neither (iii) => (ii) nor (ii) => (i); in (ii) => (i) the global hyperbolicity of Reg M comes from that of the extension. A remark, harmless.
BTZ_1.tex:1593 ('(iii) => (ii) is trivial'): confirmed; the maximality of BTZext(M) is not used, only that it is a BTZ-extension.
questions: (ii) 'a BTZ-extension of M which is Cauchy-complete': taken as a globally hyperbolic BTZ-extension (GX.BTZMax.GHExt). By l.222 and l.227 a Cauchy-complete manifold has a Cauchy surface, which is the paper's definition of global hyperbolicity; ETT's GH (causal with compact diamonds) is not derived in the library from the existence of a Cauchy surface for E0-manifolds, so it is carried explicitly. If the author reads (ii) without GH, a Cauchy-surface-implies-GH lemma for E0-manifolds is what is missing.

OQ-142 (e), (f) and OQ-152 in force as in prop_reg_complete': 'Cauchy-complete' for the extension is E0C1CauchyComplete (DEC-31/119 plus the C1 rim of DEC-107); for Reg M it is the spacelike-Lipschitz Causal.Flat.IsCauchyComplete; 'Cauchy-maximal' of Reg M is Causal.Flat.MGH.

kb_proposals: Flat transport along a bijective isometric embedding now exists for all of GH (lean-causal Cla.cover_gh_of_isIsometricEmbedding_of_surjective), MGH and IsCauchyComplete (GXScaffold.BTZ.CauchyEasy); the last two are general flat facts, candidates to move to lean-causal Causal/Flat at graduation.

An E0-morphism restricts to a flat local isometry of the regular parts (GX.BTZCauchyEasy.isLocalIsometry_regMap: RepOn from liftPropOn_iff_repOn, then E0LM.e0_flat_transition_aux in the regular charts); the converse direction (flat isometry => E0-morphism) is T-btz-common-reg-iso's CommonRegIso.

pathLength_eq_of_local generalizes lean-causal's pathLength_pulled_eq_of_local to two arbitrary chart systems: locLipAt_pulled_iff_of_eventually applies with F := phiX (c t), since LocLipAt and localDensity only read the system at the base point.
